locations.name: Oakhaven Swamp
locations.description: A fog-choked marsh of black water and dead cypress. Iron bells toll from a half-sunk Brotherhood watchtower at dusk, and the reeds hide wardens who never blink.

locations.name: River's End Docks
locations.description: A rope-tangled wharf city of stacked crates and salt smoke. Captain Vane's customs house squats on the eastern quay; smugglers swear the tide here runs backward on the new moon.

locations.name: Shrine of the Tideborn
locations.description: A drowned temple of black basalt, its altar slick with brine and older than the kingdom. Pilgrims leave coins in the shallow water and never see them again.

locations.name: Blackbriar Forest
locations.description: A thorn-choked wood where the canopy swallows daylight. Old Seraphine's wretched hut squats in a clearing of ash, and the briars grow back within the hour if cut.

lore.text: The Obsidian Brotherhood keeps its vigil in the black bogs of Oakhaven. Founded by a cult that worshiped the dead tides, they have remained silent since the Drowning Festival began. The iron bells toll not for names or events lost to time, but for those who are remembered — and those who were never given proper names at all.

The tideglass fragments are the only things that can truly track a Brotherhood warden's movements. They were not made by men, but found in the deeps of the drowned river when the tides changed for the worse. The fragments pulse with a slow, steady rhythm, and they know what is happening even if the watchers do not.

On the night of the Drowning Festival the river is supposed to give back one thing it has taken. The tradition is old, older than the kingdom, and it is kept with a gravity that makes the living uneasy. The festival is a night of black lanterns, of coins cast into the black water, of the great bell rung once for every name in the drowned village's roll. This year the roll is shorter.

The tideborn are beings of the deep, ancient and powerful. They do not speak in words but in sensations — the pull of currents, the pulse of tides, the memory of drowning. Those who hear their call may become one with the waters or be lost forever to the depths.

The Blackbriar Forest was once a peaceful woodland, but it has become twisted by something dark. The trees grow in unnatural patterns, and the roots of some are alive with black magic that reaches out to pull unwary travelers into shadowy depths.

Old Seraphine was once a respected healer in the village, but her experiments with marsh-fever have turned her into something else. She now lives in the forest clearing alone, and she speaks only to those who can provide her with more of the rare ingredients she needs for her research.

quests.title: The Swamp's Mystery
quests.description: Learn why the Brotherhood's iron bells toll for names the drowned village no longer remembers, and what the black water is counting toward.

quests.title: The Guild's Contract
quests.description: Deliver the sealed letter to Captain Vane at the River's End Docks. She will pay in coin, not favors, and she will inspect the seal before she opens it.

quests.title: Vaelen's Debt
quests.description: Vaelen owes the Shrine a life for the bell he broke. The debt is coming due, and the tideglass in your pack is the only proof it exists.

items.item_name: Chart of the River's End waterways

abilities.name: Tideglass Sense — feel the vigil bell's warmth through the fragment in your pack and know when a Brotherhood warden draws near
Wade Through Black Water — move silently through the swamp without disturbing the reeds or alerting wardens
Tideborn Healing — draw upon ancient waters to mend wounds and heal minor ailments
